newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Citibank plans $150 mln loan for Romania's Renel.
newsitem.headline: Citibank plans $150 mln loan for Romania's Renel.

text.p: Citibank said on Thursday it would arrange a $150 million syndicated loan for Romania's Renel RA electricity authority to help the state-run company fund fuel imports.

"Citibank has been mandated to raise $150 million for Renel ...for the purpose of importing fuel oil and natural gas to ensure country energy sources and needs for the coming winter," Citibank's Bucharest subsidiary said in a statement.
It said the $150 million financing would be arranged through a revolving credit facility and/or a revolving letter of credit facility for 12 months, guaranteed by the state.

Renel made its debut on the international capital markets last December when it raised a $160 million syndicated loan arranged by ING Bank. Renel used the loan to import 1.3 million tonnes of fuel oil.
During the 1995/1996 winter, an acute shortage of hard currency forced Romania to cut fuel imports and power supplies to industrial sectors.

Citibank helped Romania to rejoin world capital markets in 1995 after more than a decade of absence with syndicated loans for the central bank. It also helped the Balkan country to raise funds from the international markets to help finance the farming sector.
